svg.text: Mean copy number does not determine the loss rate
Random segregation only. Each curve is one spread in copy number across cells; the straight line is the textbook formula,
which assumes every cell carries the same number. A and B show that the curves' two parameters are not enough.
Mean copy number among plasmid-bearing cells
Chance a daughter is born plasmid-free
At a mean of 10 copies, a spread of CV 0.6
A and B: same mean (20) and same CV (0.10),
2,600× apart. Two moments are not enough.
No data and no fit: every value is computed from models/copy-number-burden/battle_royale/segregation.py
Assumes random segregation with no partition system, no multimer resolution and no selection, and a lognormal copy-number distribution across cells.
The left tail of that distribution sets every value here, so read the gaps as orders of magnitude rather than as numbers.
A reference point, not a bound: partition systems put a plasmid below these curves, multimerisation and clustering put one above.
Measured loss for ColE1-type vectors runs five to eight orders of magnitude higher than their copy number predicts (Summers & Sherratt 1984).
